item.title: Manteca will soon be down to 1 dispensary
item.description: Nectar is closing its Manteca cannabis dispensary.

item.title: Manteca Mural Society turned downtown into outdoor gallery
item.description: The Manteca Mural Society set about 24 years ago to find suitable downtown walls to turn into canvases for public art. But in reality, it is more than just art.

item.title: Opening of Terraces at Bethany topped Ripon growth in ‘25
item.description: The opening of the Terraces at Bethany was a big moment this past year in Ripon.

item.title: In Sacramento, soda is poison for kids in school but not if they benefit from SNAP
item.description: There was a time, believe it or not, soda vending machines in high schools generated thousands upon thousands of dollars for schools.

item.title: Sequoia & Kings Canyon: Two adjoining national parks showcase the beauty of the Southern Sierra
item.description: VISALIA — Largest tree by volume on earth. More pristine Sierra wilderness that in Yosemite National Park. Second deepest river gorge in the United States. The tallest peak in the Lower 48 States.

item.title: CITY LOOKING TO BUY IOOF HALL FOR $1.2M
item.description: Manteca’s elected leaders on Tuesday are expected to formally agree to a $1.2 million deal to buy one of the city’s most historic buildings that holds both cultural and architectural significance.

item.title: Hearing Tuesday final hurdle for homeless shelter
item.description: The final regulatory hurdle for starting physical work on Manteca’s permanent homeless navigation center could be cleared Tuesday. That’s when the City Council conducts a public hearing during their 6 p.m. meeting to consider approving an amendment to an existing conditional use permit at 555 Industrial Park Drive to allow the rehabilitation of onsite structures to proceed.

item.title: Naven: Manteca might be better off with 2, not 3 cannabis dispensaries
item.description: Two cannabis dispensaries may be all that Manteca needs. It’s a preliminary assessment made by mayoral hopeful Jacob Naven who is challenging incumbent Gary Singh in the November election.

item.title: Street lights: Lathrop looks to save $6M over 20 years
item.description: The City of Lathrop is looking to replace its existing High-Pressure Sodium streetlights to that of an energy-efficient light emitting diode or LED fixtures.

item.title: Ripon council approves 88 two-story homes as part of North Pointe
item.description: The Meadowood Subdivision in Ripon continues to make progress. Located on West Colony Road and Fulton Avenue, this community fitted between the Save Mart shopping center and the Mistlin Sports Park will feature 88 two-story homes, once grown out.
